Subject: Staging evaluation — proposed exit plan & verification log

Hi Ellis,

Appended is our initial mutual action plan (MAP) for the staging evaluation window. This version focuses on measurable exit gates and the verification checklist we'll run as part of the final staging sign-off. High level:

- Goal: Validate latency, token throughput, and functional correctness for the two primary flows (patient intake summarization and triage-assist).
- Staging window: 2 weeks (2026-07-06 to 2026-07-20) — tentative, pending your availability.
- Exit gates (proposed):
  1) Latency P95 <= 220ms on production-sized batches (50 concurrent users)
  2) End-to-end recall >= 92% on the 250-case prompt set (validation corpus)
  3) No critical security gaps in the infra audit (KMS/HSM verification completed)
  4) No >1 severity-1 incidents during a 72-hour observation window

I've attached MAP_v1.xlsx which has the timeline, owners, and the verification log template. Please review and flag any missing verification steps (especially from your security/compliance side).

Next steps I propose:
- You review the MAP and fill in the acceptance-owner column by Thu 07/02
- We lock the staging dates and schedule the smoke test on the first day of the window

Thanks — feel free to call if you want to walk through the plan.

Best,
Dylan

Ellis — quick technical reply with the test approach and acceptance-test scripts (high level):

1) Perf methodology (P95):
   - Load generator simulates 50 concurrent interactive users, inter-arrival times per the attached harness.
   - Each simulated user runs the two canonical flows: intake-summary (avg prompt tokens 320) and triage-assist (avg prompt tokens 140).
   - We collect token-level timing at the inference endpoint and compute P95 over a 15-minute rolling window.

2) Reproducibility: we'll share the exact k6 script and a containerized harness. Expect reproducible results within +/-5% if your infra mimics the staging config.

3) Functional acceptance tests:
   - 250-case validation corpus; we provide ground-truth labels and a scoring script (recall/F1).
   - Smoke tests: start/stop, cold-cache vs warm-cache checks, and KV cache priming runbook.

I've attached a small shell harness and the smoke checklist. Ben will be on the call for Day 2 and can run the smoke scripts with your team.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
